messages.author: fc22cb727156ff4f
messages.subject: Forcing breaks to specify labels
parts:
Hi all,

The newest version of ggplot requires breaks to be specified in scale
to be able to modify labels. While this makes sense for continuous
numeric values, I find it counter intuitive for discrete scales. Here
is an example use case

d <- data.frame(x=1:2, y=1:2, z=c("A","B"))

ggplot(d) + geom_point(aes(x=x, y=y, colour=z)) +
scale_colour_hue("Test", labels=c("foo", "bar"))
# does not work because breaks are not specified
# OK so breaks for a discrete scale should just be the levels of the
corresponding factor
ggplot(d) + geom_point(aes(x=x, y=y, colour=z)) +
scale_colour_hue("Test", breaks=levels(z), labels=c("foo", "bar"))
# but that does not work either because scale does not find z (i.e.
doest not look in d)
# So I have to specify where to look explicitly
ggplot(d) + geom_point(aes(x=x, y=y, colour=z)) +
scale_colour_hue("Test", breaks=levels(d$z), labels=c("foo", "bar"))
# OK. That works, but maybe I want to be quicker and specify only the
internal representation of the factor:
as.numeric(d$z)
# Let's try
ggplot(d) + geom_point(aes(x=x, y=y, colour=z)) +
scale_colour_hue("Test", breaks=1:2, labels=c("foo", "bar"))
# not quite

Could this requirement be relaxed for discrete scales where breaks is
necessarily levels(data)?

JiHO

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Forcing breaks to specify labels
parts:
Hi Jiho,

The problem is that the breaks might not necessarily be the levels of
the data - for various reasons they may have been dropped of, or you
may have been working with a character vector the whole time.

I implemented this change because I was concerned about the
catastrophic possibility that your labels might not be lined up with
the values you expect and you'd interpret the graph completely
incorrectly. Another way to construct the labels with a little less
typing is:

> dput(levels(d$z))
c("A", "B")

and then modify to:

c(foo = "A", bar = "B")

and supply as the breaks argument.

Hadley
